# Files the fork publishes in its own shape.
#
# .github/workflows/sync-upstream.yml rebuilds `main` as upstream + the HMCL-CN-Patch
# commit series. When a patch that edits one of these files no longer replays onto the
# new upstream (upstream changed the same lines), the replay keeps the patch's version
# instead of merging hunk by hunk, because the fork copy is meant to replace upstream's.
#
# Only list a path here when that replacement is intended, i.e. when dropping upstream's
# changes to it is what the fork wants. Everything else conflicts loudly and fails the run.
#
# Why gradle.yml: upstream runs one job per OS/JDK combination for testing; this fork
# builds once (ubuntu-latest, JDK 17) and publishes that single build, because
# publish-release.yml turns one run into exactly one release and labels it with
# BUILD_NUMBER = github.run_number.
.github/workflows/gradle.yml
